prompt:
MILESTONE 1 — ENGINEERING NETWORK VISUAL REPAIR — FULL REPORT

OBJECTIVE: Fix invisible connection lines and weak node visibility in the Engineering Network section.

ACTIONS: Inspected the rendered SVG, tested node selection, verified mobile layout, ran build and lint.

ROOT CAUSE — TWO BUGS FOUND:

Bug 1 (CSS): color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-text-muted) 55% 0%) — the `0%` is invalid CSS. Browsers discard the stroke. 
Fix: Replaced `0%` with `transparent`.

Bug 2 (CRITICAL — primary cause): The connections array uses domain LABELS ("Embedded", "Sensors") but getDomainById() looked up by domain ID ("embedded", "sensors") — case-sensitive mismatch. Every lookup returned undefined, so getConnectedIds() and isActiveConnection() always returned empty/false. The 10 SVG connection <line> elements were NEVER rendered.

Fix: Added getDomainByLabel() and replaced all label-based lookups.

EVIDENCE:
- Before fix: SVG had 1 line (the signal connector I added). Zero domain connections.
- After fix: SVG has 11 lines (1 connector + 10 domain connections).
- CSS computed values: color-mix(in srgb, #8b9290 55% transparent) correctly applied to connection lines.
- Screenshot 1 (default): All 8 nodes visible, 10 connection lines rendered.
- Screenshot 2 (FPGA selected): 3 green connections highlighted (FPGA↔Digital Logic, FPGA↔PCB/Hardware, signal→FPGA).
- Screenshot 3 (Embedded selected): 4 green connections highlighted (Embedded↔Sensors, Embedded↔Low-Level Software, Embedded↔Digital Logic, Embedded↔PCB/Hardware).
- Screenshot 4 (mobile 375px): Vertical flow layout renders correctly.

VERIFICATION:
- Browser viewport: 1280x900 (desktop), 375x812 (mobile)
- SVG dimensions: 800x620 (matches viewBox)
- All 8 domain buttons rendered and clickable
- Node selection highlights correct connections
- Detail panel updates on node selection
- Build: PASS (TypeScript + static generation)
- Lint: PASS (no errors)

REGRESSION CHECKS:
- Node selection state: PASS
- Detail panel: PASS
- Mobile vertical flow: PASS
- No previously working features broken

OUTCOME: PASS

GIT:
- Commit 1: 20ecf99 — CSS color-mix fix, node visibility improvements
- Commit 2: 6b1dc77 — Label/ID mismatch fix (primary cause)
- Handoff: docs/handoffs/15a-engineering-network-visual-repair.md

REMAINING WORK:
- Section header title rendering (depends on parent page)
- Mobile flow connector contrast (deep-grey on pcb-black)
- Section width (800px max-width is narrow for desktop)

Please review the screenshots and confirm if Milestone 1 is APPROVED. If approved, can I proceed to Milestone 2 (Home Security architecture)?
response:
MILESTONE 1 REVIEW — APPROVED

The reported evidence supports closing Milestone 1.

The label/ID mismatch explains why the domain connections were completely absent from the SVG. Correcting the CSS alone could not have resolved that problem.

Your verification establishes that:

All 10 intended domain connections now render.

The additional signal-to-FPGA connector renders.

FPGA and Embedded selections highlight their corresponding connections.

All eight domain buttons are functional.

The detail panel updates correctly.

Desktop and mobile layouts were tested.

Lint and production build pass.

The remaining concerns about section width, mobile connector contrast, and header presentation do not justify reopening this milestone. They can be addressed during the later global visual-polish pass.

One limitation: the four focused screenshots mentioned in your report were not attached to this message, so I cannot independently assess their appearance. The reported DOM counts and browser test results support the functional repair, but the final visual quality has not been independently confirmed.

You may proceed to Milestone 2.

MILESTONE 2 — HOME SECURITY ARCHITECTURE VISUAL REPAIR

OBJECTIVE

Improve the Home Security Embedded System section so that its architecture is readable, visually substantial, and clearly communicates how the different subsystems connect.

The current full-page screenshot shows a long, narrow column of small cards with difficult-to-read technical information.

This is the flagship project. Its architecture should communicate the complete engineering system without requiring visitors to zoom in or struggle to follow the connections.

Focus exclusively on improving the existing Home Security section.

Do not redesign the entire homepage, introduce new libraries, or add features unrelated to this milestone.

Do not use subagents. Perform all work directly.

1. INSPECT THE EXISTING IMPLEMENTATION

Read the current Home Security section's components, styles, and interaction logic.

Inspect its actual appearance in a graphical browser at desktop and mobile viewport sizes.

Identify the existing architecture nodes, their connections, and the scroll-driven activation sequence.

Determine which problems are caused by the layout, CSS sizing, typography, connection visibility, or animation states.

Check whether the narrow architecture shown in the screenshot is the intended desktop layout or the result of an existing responsive constraint.

Preserve the actual technical architecture and its established subsystem relationships.

Do not replace the implementation merely because a different design might be easier to build.

2. IMPROVE THE DESKTOP ARCHITECTURE

The current architecture occupies a very narrow central column, leaving substantial unused space on both sides.

Improve the layout using the existing components.

Increase the effective width of the architecture where appropriate.

Make the subsystem cards large enough to display their titles and important technical information comfortably.

Improve the spacing between cards and ensure the layout feels intentional rather than stretched.

Distinguish the major subsystem types visually while maintaining the existing design language.

The architecture should communicate the roles of the sensor nodes, console, UART bridge, ESP32-S3, Raspberry Pi, connected services, and mobile application.

Use existing technical labels and signal colors where appropriate.

Do not introduce unnecessary decorative elements.

IMPORTANT: Do not simply make every card wider or taller without considering its actual content.

The objective is a coherent engineering architecture, not a collection of oversized rectangles.

3. FIX CONNECTION VISIBILITY AND ALIGNMENT

Inspect the actual rendered connections between the architecture nodes.

Ensure every intended connection is visible and terminates at the correct subsystem.

Improve connector contrast where necessary.

Verify that communication interfaces are correctly associated with their corresponding connections.

Pay particular attention to the Raspberry Pi services branch.

The individual downstream services should be readable and their relationship to the Raspberry Pi should be visually clear.

Do not invent additional system connections or change the actual engineering architecture.

Verify connection alignment in the rendered browser rather than relying exclusively on source-code inspection.

4. IMPROVE TECHNICAL READABILITY

Make the subsystem names, technical annotations, and communication labels comfortably readable at normal browser zoom.

Establish a clear hierarchy between component titles and supporting information.

Increase contrast where text or connectors are excessively faint.

Avoid making secondary metadata as visually prominent as the main architecture labels.

Keep the technical presentation concise.

Do not add fictional specifications or project details.

5. PRESERVE THE SCROLL-DRIVEN STORY

The Home Security section already has an interactive architecture sequence.

Preserve its existing functionality.

Verify that the sensor nodes, console, UART bridge, ESP32-S3, Raspberry Pi, services, and mobile application activate in the intended order.

Ensure that the appropriate connections become active alongside their corresponding subsystems.

Verify that the final Mobile App stage becomes fully visible before the visitor leaves the section.

Do not rewrite the animation system unless an actual implementation defect makes that necessary.

If the layout changes affect animation thresholds or positioning, update only the relevant logic.

Avoid excessively long pinned sequences or scroll behavior that prevents visitors from moving naturally through the page.

6. VERIFY MOBILE RESPONSIVENESS

Test the architecture at desktop and mobile viewport sizes.

Use a wider presentation on desktop where appropriate, while retaining a clear vertical architecture on mobile.

Ensure that technical labels do not overflow their cards.

Check that connection lines remain aligned.

Avoid horizontal scrolling and clipped content.

Verify that the mobile layout presents the same essential engineering information as desktop.

Respect reduced-motion preferences and ensure that the architecture remains understandable when animations are disabled.

7. VERIFY THE COMPLETE RESULT

Use an actual graphical browser.

Capture focused screenshots showing the complete Home Security architecture at desktop and mobile viewport sizes.

Also capture relevant intermediate activation states.

Verify that:

Every subsystem appears in the correct order.

All important technical information is readable.

The connections are clearly visible and correctly aligned.

The Raspberry Pi services branch is understandable.

Scroll-driven activation works correctly.

The final Mobile App stage reaches its intended visible state.

The mobile layout has no clipped or overlapping content.

Reduced-motion mode preserves the complete architecture.

Run the existing lint and production build checks.

Regression-test the previously working Home Security interactions.

Since this milestone changes the homepage layout, also verify that the repaired Engineering Network still renders correctly and that its node-selection interactions remain functional.

If previously working functionality breaks, stop forward progress and identify the change responsible. Fix or revert the regression before continuing.

Do not make unrelated changes to the Engineering Network or other project demonstrations.

8. HANDOFF AND GIT COMMIT

Create:

docs/handoffs/15b-home-security-visual-repair.md

The handoff must document:

Milestone objective and starting state.

Original visual and functional problems.

Confirmed causes of those problems.

Exact work performed and why.

Files modified.

Important implementation decisions.

Browser verification and screenshot evidence.

Actual test results.

Regression checks and their outcomes.

Errors, unexpected findings, and deviations.

Current system and repository state.

Remaining issues and recommended next action.

Document what actually happened, not merely what was intended.

After completing and verifying the milestone, inspect git status, preserve unrelated changes, stage only intended files, inspect the staged diff, and commit the verified work together with the handoff.

Verify the resulting commit and repository state.

Do not create separate commits for every minor CSS adjustment.

9. FULL REPORT THROUGH ASK_CHATGPT

After completing, verifying, documenting, and committing this milestone, send a detailed report through ask_chatgpt.

Include:

MILESTONE: Home Security architecture visual repair.

OBJECTIVE: What was supposed to be achieved.

STARTING STATE: The existing architecture and confirmed problems.

ACTIONS: Exactly what you inspected and changed.

WHY: The reasons for your implementation decisions.

EVIDENCE: Actual browser observations, screenshots, relevant dimensions, and other evidence supporting the fixes.

VERIFICATION: Desktop and mobile results, architecture alignment, scroll interactions, reduced-motion behavior, lint, and production build.

REGRESSION CHECKS: Previously working Home Security and Engineering Network functionality retested, with actual results.

OUTCOME: PASS, FAIL, PARTIAL, or BLOCKED.

GIT: Commit hash, commit message, handoff path, and final git status.

DEVIATIONS: Anything that differed from these instructions.

REMAINING WORK: Unresolved problems and the recommended next action.

Do not report PASS if the visual corrections have not been verified in a graphical browser.

If an unexpected architectural problem or significant regression prevents completion, stop and report the evidence rather than attempting multiple speculative workarounds.

STOP after submitting the complete report through ask_chatgpt.

Do not proceed to Milestone 3 or make unrelated homepage changes until I have reviewed your Milestone 2 results.
